profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and computing company, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA. It trades on the exchange under the ticker NVDA and reported revenue of $215,938,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, according to its most recent 10-K filing. The company's work spans hardware, software, and AI infrastructure, with a significant focus on GPU-accelerated computing for enterprise and research applications.

On the AI side, NVIDIA develops the Nemotron family of multimodal foundation models, which the company describes as designed for agentic AI workflows involving reasoning, vision, speech, retrieval-augmented generation, and safety tasks. Nemotron models are built on top of existing open frontier models and are made available with published weights, training datasets, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, a permissive license that permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without requiring attribution to NVIDIA. Specific models and tools mentioned on the site include Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, NeMo Switchyard, NVIDIA NeMo, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA Dynamo, and support for open-source libraries such as SGLang and vLLM. Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site in connection with the vision behind Nemotron. The company also tracks ServiceNow as a partner that has evaluated Nemotron's visual question-and-answer accuracy.

NVIDIA's second tracked AI product is NVIDIA NIM, a set of inference microservices for deploying foundation models in enterprise environments with GPU optimization and self-hosted deployment options. NIM microservices for Nemotron are available through build.nvidia.com and require an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for production use, while trial access is offered at no license requirement. The held facts record no litigation or MCP server presence for NVIDIA at this time.
